steps.prompt: what was the idea about kindness inward?
steps.answer: kindness inward isn't going easy. it tends to go along with greater well-being.

steps.text: let's look at what's already good. no modesty needed here.
strengths aren't trophies. they're the things done naturally, often without noticing.

steps.prompt: which of these fit, even a little?
options: i stay calm when it counts
steps.reply: kept in the book, under about me. they were there all along.

steps.text: in the early 2000s, psychologists gathered a list of 24 character strengths, like kindness, humor and curiosity, from writing across many cultures and centuries.
steps.evidence: a widely used way to describe strengths

steps.text: when did one of these show up lately, even in a tiny way?

options.label: today
options.reply: lovely. small counts. it's still you.

options.label: this week
options.reply: then it's alive and well, whether or not anyone noticed.

options.label: can't think of one
options.reply: that's okay. strengths are easy to miss up close. keep an eye out today.

ideas: kept going when it was hard.

steps.text: using a strength in a new way, on purpose, lifted happiness in one well-known study. later studies found smaller effects, but it's an easy thing to try.
use one strength on purpose today, in a small new way.

grounding.idea: using signature strengths in a new way increased happiness in a randomized online study
grounding.source: Seligman, Steen, Park & Peterson, 2005, American Psychologist
